name: Piper J-5 Cub Cruiser
summary: Wider, three-seat development of the J-3 Cub with the pilot in front and a bench seat for two behind; the later J-5C became the PA-12.

wings: High wing braced by a single strut per side
engines: Single small flat-four, cowled on later models
fuselage: Wider fabric fuselage than a J-3 with a rear bench seat
Three-seat cabin with large side windows
Fixed main gear with a tailwheel

tellTales: Strut-braced high-wing with a conspicuously wider cabin than its tandem cousins
Rounded, rolled-edge tail over a tailwheel
Strut-braced wing on a small, three-seat fabric aircraft

confusedWith.howToTell: The J-5 is wider with a bench seat for two behind the pilot; the J-3 is a narrow tandem aircraft.
The J-5 is the earlier, less-cowled version; the PA-12 has a fully enclosed cowl, metal-spar wing and a smoother engine installation.
The J-5 has a wider three-seat cabin; the PA-11 is a narrow tandem two-seater.
The J-5 is a small three-seater with a rounded Cub tail; the Stinson 108 is a larger four-seater with a six-cylinder nose.
